lessonRef.unitTitle: PF3 — Budgeting and Saving: Running the Adult Budget
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: irregular income and cash-flow timing

objective: Establish that a fictional irregular income covers its obligations in total, find the months in which it does not, and size the buffer that timing alone requires.
scenario: The simulated six-month income record below belongs to a fictional worker paid per project. Every figure is invented for this exercise.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional income record in these directions

tasks.directions: Over 6 months the fictional worker received $1,850, $4,320, $900, $3,780, $2,640, and $4,110. Fixed obligations are $2,470 every month and fall due whether or not a payment has arrived.

prompts.text: What did the 6 months bring in altogether?
What is the average monthly income across the 6 months?
What do the fixed obligations come to over the same 6 months?

tasks.directions: Now find the months the average conceals.

prompts.text: What surplus did the 6 months produce in total?
In the weakest month, income was $900. What was the position in that month alone?
How much must be held in reserve to carry that month without borrowing?
Month 1 also fell short, on income of $1,850 against the same obligations. What was the position in month 1?
Across the whole 6 months, is the income sufficient to meet the obligations?
choices: Yes — but only if the timing is bridged
No — the income falls short over the period

prompts.text: This income is sufficient over 6 months and insufficient in two of them. Explain why an average of $2,933.33 is a misleading basis for planning here, and describe how you would run this budget so that both short months are survivable — naming what your method requires the worker to do in a strong month, and what has to be in place before month 1.

remediation: Use the fictional scenario and work one graded prompt at a time. For each number response, copy the given fictional quantities into integer cents, choose the operation the wording calls for, calculate, and check the result with an inverse operation or estimate. For each choice response, test every option against the stated facts and eliminate an option only when a fact rules it out. For each written response, make a claim and support it with at least one detail from the fictional scenario. Use these steps to check the method while keeping every final result in your own response.
extension: After submitting the graded work, change one invented amount or assumption in the scenario. Rework the affected response using integer cents whenever money is involved, then explain whether and why the written judgment changes. Keep the variation fictional and do not use real household information.
